record.field: purpose: confirm that one or more minions respond on Salt when: first step in any troubleshooting — verify connectivity before further diagnosis when not: for fetching data (use pillar/grains/service-status instead) example: {"minion": "gw*"} or {"minion": "*"} for all output: True/False per minion ID guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
{"type":"object","properties":{"minion":{"type":"string","description":"Minion ID or glob (e.g. '*' for all, 'gw*' for gateways)","default":"*"}},"required":[]}
async def execute(minion="*"): """Ping Salt minion(s).""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "test.ping")

purpose: apply a Salt state on minions and change system configuration when: after diagnosis, when the action is confirmed and the state exists (e.g. 'caddy.service') when not: for inspection (use salt_state_show_sls first); require approval before example: {"minion": "gw*", "state": "caddy.service"} output: state result per minion (retcode, changes, comment) guardrail: requires human approval (destructive)

{"type":"object","properties":{"minion":{"type":"string","description":"Minion glob"},"state":{"type":"string","description":"State to apply (e.g. 'caddy.service')"},"pillar":{"type":"string","description":"Extra pillar as JSON string (optional)","default":""}},"required":["minion","state"]}

purpose: apply ALL states according to top.sls on minions — full convergence when: when a minion has drifted broadly and normal state.apply is not enough when not: for single changes (use salt_state_apply); very broad impact example: {"minion": "gw*"} output: highstate result per minion (retcode, changes per state) guardrail: requires human approval (destructive, long-running timeout 600s)
async def execute(minion): """Run highstate.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "state.highstate", timeout=600)

purpose: show how a state compiles for a minion — validation before applying when: before salt_state_apply, to verify the state applies and compiles when not: for changing anything (read-only); for running the state (use salt_state_apply) example: {"minion": "gw1", "state": "caddy.service"} output: compiled SLS per minion with any error messages guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion, state): """Show compiled SLS.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "state.show_sls", state)

purpose: run a shell command on minions — diagnosis and simple operations when: when the Salt tools are not enough (e.g. 'df -h', 'systemctl list-units', 'ps aux') when not: for standard queries (use the service/disk/memory/process tools); full shell access example: {"minion": "gw1", "command": "systemctl status caddy | head -20"} output: command stdout/stderr per minion guardrail: requires human approval (destructive — arbitrary execution)
async def execute(minion, command): """Run shell command on minion.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "cmd.run", command)

purpose: fetch a specific pillar key from a minion (configuration) when: to read configuration values (e.g. bifrost, odoo, mail settings) when not: for system information (use grains); pillar may contain secrets example: {"minion": "gw1", "key": "odoo"} output: the pillar value for the key, or null if missing guardrail: none — but handle output carefully (secrets in pillar)
async def execute(minion, key): """Fetch pillar data.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "pillar.get", key)

purpose: fetch ALL pillar data from a minion — complete configuration picture when: when the whole picture is needed (e.g. troubleshooting where a setting comes from) when not: for single keys (use salt_pillar_get); large output example: {"minion": "gw1"} output: complete pillar dictionary guardrail: none — but handle output carefully (secrets in pillar)
async def execute(minion): """Fetch all pillar data.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "pillar.items")

purpose: fetch a specific grain (system facts) from a minion when: for OS/role/network information (e.g. 'os', 'dc', 'roles', 'customer') when not: for configuration (use pillar); for all facts (use grains_items) example: {"minion": "gw1", "key": "roles"} output: the grain value for the key guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion, key): """Fetch specific grain.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "grains.get", key)

purpose: fetch ALL grains from a minion — OS, CPU, memory, network, roles when: to build a picture of an unknown minion (which role, which OS, customer) when not: for single facts (use grains_get); large output example: {"minion": "gw1"} output: complete grain dictionary guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion): """Fetch all grains.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "grains.items")

purpose: list all Salt minions — accepted, unaccepted, rejected when: to find minions, see if a new minion is waiting for approval when not: for status of individual minions (use test_ping/service) example: {} (no parameters) output: lists per status (accepted/unaccepted/rejected) guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(): """List all minions.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("runner", None, "minions.list")

purpose: accept a new minion key so it can be managed when: when a new minion has appeared in minion_list under unaccepted and should be put into operation when not: for existing minions; requires confirmation first (security impact) example: {"minion_id": "gw3"} output: key.accept result guardrail: requires human approval (destructive — key management)
async def execute(minion_id): """Accept minion key.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("wheel", None, "key.accept", minion_id)

purpose: check the status of a systemd service on a minion when: during an outage — is the service active/inactive/failed? when not: for changing the service (use service_restart); for other service tools example: {"minion": "gw1", "service": "caddy"} output: service status (active/inactive/failed etc.) guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion, service): """Check service status.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "service.status", service)

purpose: restart a systemd service on minions when: after diagnosis, when a service is failed and a restart is the right action when not: without diagnosis first (check service_status + journal_errors); frequently example: {"minion": "gw1", "service": "caddy"} output: restart result (active after restart) guardrail: requires human approval (destructive — service interruption)
async def execute(minion, service): """Restart service.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "service.restart", service)

purpose: check disk space on a minion (df -h) when: on disk warnings, space problems, cleanup needs when not: for processes/memory (use process_list/memory_usage) example: {"minion": "gw1", "path": "/var"} — empty path = all output: df -h output per minion guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion, path=""): """Check disk usage.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] cmd = f"df -h {path}" if path else "df -h" return api.salt_call("local", minion, "cmd.run", cmd)

purpose: check memory usage on a minion (free -m) when: on suspected OOM, memory leaks, performance problems when not: for disk (use disk_usage); for processes (use process_list) example: {"minion": "gw1"} output: free -m output per minion guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion): """Check memory usage.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "cmd.run", "free -m")

purpose: check system load (load average) via uptime when: on high load, performance diagnosis, root cause investigation when not: for detailed CPU (use cmd_run 'top -bn1'); for memory/disk example: {"minion": "gw1"} output: uptime output (load 1/5/15) per minion guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(minion): """Check system load.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.salt_call("local", minion, "cmd.run", "uptime")

purpose: fetch the latest errors from the systemd journal on a minion when: on service failure — what did the service log before it fell? when not: for the full log (use cmd_run 'journalctl'); for realtime reading example: {"minion": "gw1", "unit": "odoo", "lines": 50} — empty unit = all output: latest journal lines with errors guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

async def execute(minion, unit="", lines=50): """Fetch journal errors.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] cmd = f"journalctl -p err -n {lines}" if unit: cmd += f" -u {unit}" cmd += " --no-pager" return api.salt_call("local", minion, "cmd.run", cmd)

purpose: list processes on a minion, filtered by name when: to find processes (e.g. odoo/postgres), duplicate starts, zombies when not: for resource usage (use memory/load); for service status example: {"minion": "gw1", "filter": "odoo"} — empty filter = top 20 output: process list (PID, name, possibly CPU/memory) guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

purpose: fetch active alerts/problems from Zabbix, filtered by severity when: to see current drift alerts — what is alerting right now? when not: for history (use get_problems/get_history); for acknowledging (acknowledge) example: {"severity": "high", "limit": 20} output: list of active alerts with host, trigger, severity guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

{"type":"object","properties":{"severity":{"type":"string","description":"Severity: high, medium, low, all","default":"high"},"limit":{"type":"integer","description":"Max number of results","default":20}},"required":[]}

async def execute(severity="high", limit=20): """Fetch Zabbix alerts.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] sev_map = {"high":[4,5],"medium":[3],"low":[0,1,2],"all":[0,1,2,3,4,5]} sev = sev_map.get(severity, [4,5]) result = api.call("problem.get", { "output": "extend", "severities": sev, "recent": True, "sortfield": ["eventid"], "sortorder": "DESC", "limit": limit, }) return str(result)

purpose: fetch information about a specific Zabbix host when: for host details (interfaces, status, groups) during investigation when not: for problems on the host (use get_problems/get_alerts) example: {"host": "gw1"} output: host information (name, status, interfaces) guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

purpose: fetch all Zabbix problems including historical — deeper than get_alerts when: for the full problem picture, including older problems, per host when not: for a quick overview (use get_alerts); for metrics (get_history) example: {"host": "gw1", "recent": "true", "limit": 50} output: problem list with event, trigger, host, times guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

purpose: acknowledge a Zabbix alert with a comment about the action when: AFTER the action has been taken and verified — document what was done when not: before the action; to hide unresolved problems example: {"event_id": "123456", "message": "Restarted caddy on gw1, verified active"} output: acknowledge result guardrail: requires human approval (write — changes alert status)

{"type":"object","properties":{"event_id":{"type":"string","description":"Zabbix event ID to acknowledge"},"message":{"type":"string","description":"Comment about the action","default":"Acknowledged by Infrastructure Operator"}},"required":["event_id"]}

purpose: fetch historical metric values from a Zabbix item — trend analysis when: to see development over time (memory, load, disk) during troubleshooting when not: for current values (use get_item/get_alerts) example: {"item_id": "34567", "limit": 100} output: time series with measurement points guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

async def execute(item_id, limit=100): """Fetch historical metric values.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] result = api.call("history.get", { "output": "extend", "itemids": [item_id], "sortfield": "clock", "sortorder": "DESC", "limit": limit, }) return str(result)

purpose: fetch a Zabbix item (metric definition) for a host when: to find an item ID/key before get_history or understand what is measured when not: for metric values (use get_history); for problems (get_alerts) example: {"host": "gw1", "key_pattern": "odoo.process.count"} output: item information (key, type, last value) guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe

purpose: fetch all Zabbix host groups — infrastructure organization when: to understand how the infrastructure is divided (customer, environment, service) when not: for host details (use get_host/get_item) example: {} (no parameters) output: list of host groups guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
async def execute(): """Fetch Zabbix host groups.""" api = env['saltstack.ai.config'] return api.zabbix_call("hostgroup.get", {"output": "extend"})

purpose: fetch Zabbix triggers with status — which are active/alerting/ok when: for the trigger picture per host, see which rules are in problem when not: for active alerts (use get_alerts — faster); for metrics example: {"host": "gw1", "only_problem": "true"} output: trigger list with status per trigger guardrail: none — pure read operation, safe
